title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
data_curation: Three open-ended generation tasks use offline preference datasets D={(x, y_w, y_l)}. (1) Controlled sentiment: IMDb review prefixes (2-8 tokens); 25k prefixes, 4 completions sampled each, 6 preference pairs per prefix labeled by a pre-trained sentiment classifier (siebert/sentiment-roberta-large-english) used as ground-truth reward; GPT-2-large SFT'd 1 epoch on IMDb. (2) Summarization: Reddit TL;DR dataset with human preferences gathered by Stiennon et al.; SFT model fine-tuned on human-written forum summaries (CarperAI/openai_summarize_tldr_sft). (3) Single-turn dialogue: Anthropic Helpful-and-Harmless dataset (~170k dialogues), each ending with a response pair plus a human preference label; no SFT available, so an off-the-shelf LM is fine-tuned on preferred completions to form the reference. DPO reuses public preference datasets rather than sampling new pairs, initializing pi_ref=pi_SFT when available.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper, but DPO reshapes the standard RLHF pipeline, which the authors frame as three phases: SFT, then preference sampling + reward learning, then RL optimization. DPO collapses the latter two into a single maximum-likelihood stage over preferences. Effective order: pre-train -> SFT (to get pi_SFT) -> DPO (replacing explicit reward model + PPO). When pi_SFT is unavailable, pi_ref is initialized by maximizing likelihood of preferred completions to mitigate distribution shift. No multi-stage RL, self-play, or anneal schedule; beta controls KL strength (beta=0.1 default, 0.5 for TL;DR) and the RMSprop learning rate is linearly warmed to 1e-6 over 150 steps.
method: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) replaces the reward-model + RL stages of RLHF with one classification loss. Starting from the KL-constrained reward-maximization objective max E[r(x,y)] - beta*KL(pi||pi_ref), the optimal policy has closed form pi*(y|x) ~ pi_ref(y|x) exp(r(x,y)/beta). Rearranging gives r(x,y) = beta*log(pi*(y|x)/pi_ref(y|x)) + beta*log Z(x); under the Bradley-Terry (or Plackett-Luce) preference model the partition function cancels in reward differences, so preference probability depends only on the policy. The DPO loss is L = -E[log sigma(beta*log(pi_theta(y_w|x)/pi_ref(y_w|x)) - beta*log(pi_theta(y_l|x)/pi_ref(y_l|x)))] -- a binary cross-entropy increasing y_w and decreasing y_l likelihood, with an implicit-reward-based per-example weight that prevents the degeneration a naive ratio objective suffers. No LM sampling, no explicit reward model, no RL loop; Theorem 1 shows the reparameterization loses no reward-class generality.
eval_metrics: Controlled sentiment (IMDb, GPT-2-large): reward-vs-KL frontier under the ground-truth sentiment classifier; DPO dominates PPO and even oracle PPO-GT at every KL. Summarization (TL;DR, GPT-J 6B): GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314) win rate vs reference summaries; DPO ~61% at temp 0.0 vs PPO 57% at its best temp, more temperature-robust, beating Best-of-N. OOD on CNN/DailyMail: DPO 0.36/0.31 vs PPO 0.26/0.23 (temp 0/0.25). Dialogue (Anthropic-HH, Pythia-2.8B): GPT-4 win rate vs preferred test responses; DPO is the only efficient method beating the dataset's chosen responses, matching Best-of-128. A human study on TL;DR confirms GPT-4 agrees with humans about as often as humans agree with each other; humans preferred DPO (temp 0.25) over PPO (temp 0) 58% of the time. Models up to 6B parameters.
key_results: TL;DR summarization: DPO ~61% GPT-4 win rate vs reference (temp 0.0), beating PPO's 57% and Best-of-N; OOD CNN/DailyMail DPO 0.36 vs PPO 0.26. IMDb sentiment: DPO achieves the best reward-KL frontier, dominating PPO and oracle PPO-GT. Human eval: DPO (temp 0.25) preferred over PPO (temp 0) 58% of the time.
evolution_note: DPO (2023) builds on the RLHF pipeline of Christiano (2017), Stiennon (2022) and InstructGPT/Ouyang (2022), reacting against the complexity and instability of PPO-based RLHF by deriving the KL-constrained optimum in closed form. It replaced the reward-model-plus-RL recipe with a single cross-entropy loss, enabling a family of simpler preference-optimization methods (IPO, KTO, SLiC) and becoming a default alignment stage in later post-training stacks.
